newsitem.title: CANADA: Abitibi-Price, Stone-Consolidated agree to merge.
newsitem.headline: Abitibi-Price, Stone-Consolidated agree to merge.

text.p: Abitibi-Price Inc. and Stone-Consolidated Corp. said on Friday they agreed to merge the two big Canadian newsprint companies in an all-stock-swap transaction.

Under the agreement, each common share of Toronto-based Abitibi-Price will be exchanged for one common share of the merged company, Abitibi-Consolidated Inc. and each common share of Stone-Consolidated will be exchanged for 1.0062 common shares of Abitibi-Consolidated.

The companies said Ronald Oberlander, chairman and chief executive officer of Abitibi-Price, will be operating chairman of Abitibi-Consolidated. James Doughan, president and chief executive of Stone-Consolidated, will become president and chief executive officer of the new merged company.

Stone Container Corp., of Chicago, which owns 46.6 percent of Stone Consolidated, has agreed to vote in favour of the transaction, and after the merger would hold about 25 percent of Abitibi-Consolidated, the companies said. The transaction is expected to close in the second quarter.

The merged company would have a market capitalization of about C$4.1 billion ($3.1 billion) and annual revenues of about C$4.9 billion ($3.6 billion). The companies said they identified cost savings of more than C$100 million ($74 million) annually resulting from the merger.

Abitibi-Consolidated would have 18 paper mills, including 14 in Canada, three in the United States and one in the United Kingdom, with annual newsprint production of more than 3.2 million metric tons, making it the world's largest newsprint maker by a margin of almost two-to-one.
